rows.what: Ivone's alien file — or her father's, which would name every child
rows.note: RAISED 16 September, from David's question: a woman naturalised out of Lourenço Marques would have a file naming her parents, wouldn't she? THE RECORD CLASS IS REAL AND THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER TESTED IT. A South African naturalisation memorial asks for date and place of birth, THE FATHER'S NAME AND NATIONALITY, the date and ship of arrival, and the wife and children by name and age. AND THE FATHER'S FILE WOULD BE BETTER THAN HERS — it names every child, so it would give her parents AND her siblings in one document, which nothing this archive has tried can do. BUT THE LAW MAY HAVE REMOVED HER OWN FILE BEFORE IT EXISTED. An alien woman who married a British subject before 2 September 1949 acquired his nationality automatically; the South African Citizenship Act 44 of 1949 ended that and required an alien wife to naturalise like a man. IVONE MARRIED JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DE WITT ON 2 FEBRUARY 1948, nineteen months inside the old rule. If de Witt was a Union national she became one by marriage and there is no file for her — AND NATIONALITY ACQUIRED BY MARRIAGE SURVIVED THE DIVORCE, so TPD 534/1948 does not undo it. THAT MAKES DE WITT'S OWN NATIONALITY A QUESTION WORTH ANSWERING, because it decides whether her file can exist. THE GAZETTE HAS ALREADY BEEN SWEPT: 1930 to 1960, every year, surname Figueiredo, South African issues only — no naturalisation notice, with the control test run first and passing. On /negatives/. NAAIRS, which indexes the SAB naturalisation files, WAS UNREACHABLE on the day. The enquiry is queued for Ms Xaba as Q5 of request 24, framed as 'is there an index entry for the surname' rather than 'find her file'.

rows.what: Two Figueiredo estates found in the gazette — one of them from Lourenço Marques
rows.note: FOUND 16 September as a by-product of the naturalisation sweep, and neither was known to this archive. ESTATE 7029/54 — FIGUEIREDO, AGOSTINHO VICENTE SEBASTIAO, of Johannesburg, first and final account advertised 22 July 1955. ESTATE 2910/60 — MONTEIRO, JOSÉ DE FIGUEIREDO, OF LOURENÇO MARQUES, PORTUGUESE EAST AFRICA, executor Frederick William Damant c/o Standard Bank, advertised 2 December 1960. THE SECOND IS THE INTERESTING ONE: a man of Lourenço Marques whose estate was administered in the Union, in the decade after Ivone's marriages, which is exactly the profile of somebody the family might have known or been. NEITHER IS CLAIMED AS A RELATIVE — Figueiredo is a common Portuguese surname and 'Monteiro, José de Figueiredo' is a different name from hers. What makes them worth a row is that each has an estate number, and a South African estate file holds a death notice, form J294, which asks for the deceased's parents. THE CHEAP NEXT STEP IS THE GAZETTE, NOT THE FILE: an estate is advertised more than once, and the earlier notices carry the date of death and often the address.

rows.what: The six spellings of her name — write them down once, and put them in front of anyone searching
rows.note: RAISED 16 September on David's suggestion, and it is the kind of thing that decides whether a search works. IVONE IS RECORDED UNDER SIX SPELLINGS OF HER MAIDEN SURNAME ACROSS FIVE DOCUMENTS, and NAAIRS itself carries two of the worst. FORENAME: IVONE in most files, YVONNE in TPD 534/1948, IVONNE in WLD 2225/1953. MAIDEN SURNAME: FIGUEIREDO and DE FIGUEIREDO; MOTA FIGUEIREDO in WLD 1950/1948; DE FIGUERIDO in WLD 2225/1953; DE FIGUEREDO on her own 1953 marriage register; and FIGARETTO in the NAAIRS index. MARRIED SURNAMES: DE WITT from February 1948, LUWINSKI — also LUWINSKY and LUWENSKI — from June 1948, SALKOW from February 1953. THE PROOF THAT IT MATTERS IS THE FILE MS XABA HAS OFFERED TO CHECK: WLD 2545/1950 hid from this archive for weeks because the index spells her LUWENSKI. The table now goes into reply 21, framed as saving her a search rather than instructing her. IT ALSO COST THIS ARCHIVE A NEGATIVE: the gazette naturalisation sweep had searched only three of the six spellings. RE-RUN THE SAME DAY across all six plus the married names — no naturalisation notice under any of them, and FIGARETTO, FIGUEIRIDO and LUWENSKI turn out to appear NOWHERE IN ANY AFRICAN GAZETTE, which makes them index corruptions rather than spellings anyone ever printed. The negative on /negatives/ is corrected and is now stronger than when it was first written, not weaker.

rows.what: The names page — every spelling she is filed under, on the site rather than in a commit message
rows.note: DONE 16 September on David's instruction: 'can you also make sure the site is clear on the different spellings'. NEW PAGE /names/, in the primary nav after Ivone, with data in site/src/data/names.json. FOURTEEN FORMS, each given with the record it comes from and marked as either a document variant or an index corruption — a distinction that matters, because an index corruption tells you about the cataloguer and a document variant tells you about the family. Three forenames: IVONE, YVONNE (TPD 534/1948), IVONNE (WLD 2225/1953). Six maiden surnames: FIGUEIREDO, DE FIGUEIREDO, MOTA FIGUEIREDO (WLD 1950/1948, the fullest anybody wrote and the only record giving her a second family name), DE FIGUERIDO (WLD 2225/1953), DE FIGUEREDO (her own 1953 marriage register, written by a clerk with her standing there), FIGARETTO (the NAAIRS index). Five married: DE WITT, LUWINSKI, LUWINSKY, LUWENSKI, SALKOW. THE PAGE LEADS WITH WHAT IT COST: WLD 2545/1950 is the only action in which she is the plaintiff and it went unfound for months because the index carries her as IVONE LUWENSKI BORN FIGARETTO. It also states the rule now worked to — no surname search counts as done until every recorded spelling has been tried — AND THE COUNTER-RULE, that FIGARETTO and LUWENSKI appear nowhere in any African gazette, so a spelling that finds a file can still be one nobody ever wrote: useful for searching, useless as evidence. Cross-linked from /ivone/, and the other lines' variants (Kurt; Wear/Weir/Ware; Booyzen/Booysen/Booijzen/Booijsen) listed so the problem is not treated as hers alone.

rows.what: Re-run every source on every spelling — the sweep David asked for
rows.note: RAISED AND PART-DONE 16 September: 'all those spelling differences should now go and research everything we have to-date with the different variations'. DONE SO FAR. (1) UNION GAZETTE, 1930-1960, every year, six maiden spellings plus the married names — no naturalisation notice under any of them; FIGARETTO, FIGUEIRIDO and LUWENSKI return NOTHING ANYWHERE IN ANY AFRICAN GAZETTE. On /negatives/. (2) GENDATABASE, twelve name forms fully paged — 27 National-Archives rows that the archive's own naairs-figueiredo.tsv does not contain. The haul includes SEVEN IMMIGRATION-PAPERS FILES under Figueiredo and Figueredo, all at KAB in the IRC and PIO series, none of them hers but PROVING THE RECORD CLASS EXISTS AND IS INDEXED; and MORRIS ISAAC SALKOW'S ENTIRE LITIGATION HISTORY — TPD 467/1950, TPD 2854/1960, WLD 1593/1962, WLD 3317/1963, WLD 15934/1979, and his estate papers at KAB MOOC 6/9/5171 61416 — for the man Ivone married in February 1953 and had left by the end of it. Also OPPOSED APPLICATION. PAULA LUWINSKI VERSUS PHILLIP CRYSTAL, TAB WLD 2451/1972, a Luwinski forename this archive has not seen. (3) NAAIRS, on the corrected endpoint: FIGUEIREDO 43, FIGARETTO 1, LUWENSKI 1, LUWINSKY 1 — each variant surfacing a file the correct spelling does not return. STILL TO DO: FamilySearch, now signed in again, on all fourteen forms; the remaining ten spellings against NAAIRS; and the Salkow and Paula Luwinski finds worked up properly rather than logged. COMPLETED 16 September for NAAIRS and gendatabase. FORTY-ONE SPELLINGS TESTED — twenty-one ways of writing Figueiredo and twenty of writing Luwinski, INCLUDING MANY INVENTED ON PURPOSE to see whether a clerk had ever made the same slip. ONE GENUINELY NEW RECORD, AND IT IS A GOOD ONE: TAB MHG 7029/54, the Johannesburg estate of a Portuguese man the Union Gazette advertises as FIGUEIREDO, AGOSTINHO VICENTE SEBASTIAO and NAAIRS files as FIQUEIREDO — WITH A Q. Two indexes, two spellings, one man, and nobody had ever typed the Q. Also KAB PIO 990/42707E, IMMIGRATION PAPERS JG DE FIQUEIREDO, and SAB BAL 7, a temporary permit for a Goanese C FIGUERDO — which together prove the permit and immigration series are indexed and reachable. HE IS NOT CLAIMED AS KIN: Figueiredo is common and nothing connects him to Ivone but a city and a decade. What his file carries is a death notice, and a death notice names parents. AND ONE REAL EXCLUSION, worth as much as a find. Kurt came out of East Prussia and the slide from LUWINSKI to LEWINSKI is exactly the slide a clerk makes; there is a Lewinski and a Lewinsky family in Johannesburg in the same decades — Erwin, Bella born Berman, Meinhard, Ingeborg Ursula born Leske. THEY ARE NOT THIS FAMILY, and that is now recorded so it is never re-opened as a hopeful possibility. Seventeen invented spellings returned nothing anywhere, which is itself the finding that THE LUWINSKI NAME CORRUPTS IN ONLY TWO DIRECTIONS, NOT TEN. All of it is on /names/.

rows.what: FINDMYPAST — full subscription, one month, EXPIRES ABOUT 16 OCTOBER 2026
rows.note: DAVID TOOK A ONE-MONTH FULL SUBSCRIPTION ON 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 AND OPENED IT IN THE BROWSER. THE CLOCK IS THE POINT: everything that needs Findmypast should be done inside the window, and this row exists so that the window is not discovered to have closed. IT IS THE BEST INSTRUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER HAD FOR THE WEAR LINE, because that line is entirely English and Findmypast holds what FreeBMD and the GRO index do not. PRIORITY ORDER. (1) PASSENGER LISTS LEAVING THE UK, BT27, 1890-1960 — THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE TARGET IN THE WHOLE SUBSCRIPTION. The Wear family emigrated entire and this archive has never dated it. An outbound list gives the ship, the date, the destination port, the ages and THE WHOLE PARTY TRAVELLING TOGETHER, which would settle in one document whether Leonard went with his parents or followed. (2) THE 1939 REGISTER, which carries EXACT DATES OF BIRTH, not just quarters. If Leonard is absent from it he had already gone by September 1939; if he is present, it dates his departure to between then and his Rosebank marriage in September 1940. Either answer is worth having, and the register would also give Henry Robert and Martha Maud's exact dates. (3) BRITISH NEWSPAPER ARCHIVE — Hitchin and Letchworth titles, for Wear and Castle notices: births, marriages, deaths, court, emigration send-offs. (4) ELECTORAL REGISTERS for 72 Pix Road, Letchworth, and the years either side, to bracket the departure from the other end. (5) PARISH REGISTERS AND BAPTISMS for the six Hitchin children 1917-1936, which may name godparents and addresses the GRO index cannot. (6) THE CASTLE LINE — Martha Maud Castle's own origins, still thin. (7) PROBATE AND WILLS. HARVEST RATHER THAN BROWSE: save what is found into data/ as it goes, because the subscription ends and the evidence should not.

rows.what: TAB MHG 7029/54 — the estate found behind a Q
rows.note: FOUND 16 September by testing FIQUEIREDO, a spelling that appears in no document this archive holds and was tried only because David said to search every variation. NAAIRS: FIQUEIREDO, AGOSTINHO VICENTE SEBASTIAO, ZA TAB MHG 7029/54. The Union Gazette of 22 July 1955 advertises the first and final account in the same estate under FIGUEIREDO. THE TWO INDEXES DISAGREE ABOUT THE MAN'S NAME, which is why he has been invisible. WHAT HE IS NOT: a proven relative. Figueiredo is among the commonest Portuguese surnames and nothing ties him to Ivone except Johannesburg and the 1950s. WHAT MAKES HIM WORTH A ROW: an MHG estate file contains a death notice, form J294, and that form asks for the deceased's parents, his place of birth, and his surviving spouse and children. IF HE IS KIN, IT NAMES THE GENERATION THIS ARCHIVE CANNOT REACH; if he is not, one J294 closes him off for good. HE DIED IN 1954, six years after Ivone's Johannesburg marriages, in the same Portuguese community of the same city. CHEAP FIRST STEP BEFORE ORDERING ANYTHING: the gazette carries estates more than once, and the earlier notice gives the date of death and usually an address. Do that before spending a researcher's hour on it.

rows.what: The Portuguese are filed at Cape Town, not Pretoria — a corrected assumption
rows.note: FOUND 16 September as a by-product of the spelling sweep, and it changes where to ask. ACROSS EVERY FIGUEIREDO, FIQUEIREDO, FIGUEREDO, FIGUERIDO AND FIGUEIRA SEARCH, THE IMMIGRATION RECORDS CLUSTER IN ONE PLACE: KAB, the Cape Town Archives Repository, in the PIO series (Principal Immigration Officer) and IRC (immigration control). Sixteen of the forty Figueira records sit there; so do JG de Fiqueiredo at PIO 990/42707E, HA Figueired at PIO 33143E, Juonet Figueredo at IRC 1/4/19, Maria T Figueredo at IRC 1/3/1, and five further Figueiredos. NOT ONE OF THEM IS IVONE. WHAT IT CORRECTS: this archive had assumed naturalisation and alien files were central-government records at SAB in Pretoria, and the draft to Ms Xaba asked her for exactly that. A request pointed at the wrong depot comes back empty FOR THE WRONG REASON, which is the most expensive kind of negative there is. THE LETTER IS AMENDED to say what was actually observed and to ask the better question: whether there is a TRANSVAAL equivalent for someone who came in overland from Lourenço Marques rather than by sea to Cape Town. Ivone's route matters here — Mozambique borders the Transvaal, and a woman arriving that way may never have passed a Cape Town immigration officer at all. NEXT: put the variant spellings to the KAB PIO and IRC series directly, and ask the Western Cape Archives, where this archive already has an open request.

rows.what: THE WEAR EMIGRATION IS DATED — two ships, April and August 1939
rows.note: FOUND 16 September 2026, within the first hour of the Findmypast subscription, in BT 27 — the outbound passenger lists. THIS ARCHIVE HAS ASKED SINCE THE BEGINNING WHEN THE WEARS LEFT ENGLAND AND HAS NEVER BEEN ABLE TO ANSWER IT. HENRY ROBERT WENT FIRST, ALONE. Mr H R Wear, born 1890, aged 49, occupation MACHINE MINDER (the transcriber read it as 'machine minister'), sailed from LONDON ON 5 APRIL 1939 aboard the Union-Castle liner DURBAN CASTLE for the Cape. TNA/BT27/1540/00/0042 entry 00189. He is the only Wear on that manifest. MARTHA MAUD FOLLOWED FOUR MONTHS LATER WITH FOUR CHILDREN. On 10 AUGUST 1939 the DUNVEGAN CASTLE left London for Durban, 406 passengers, master A Alderson. FIVE WEARS IN FIVE CONSECUTIVE ENTRIES on TNA/BT27/1542/00/0024: 00223 MRS M WEAR b.1895; 00227 MISS K WEAR b.1921 age 18; 00224 MISS C WEAR b.1931 age 8; 00225 MISS L WEAR b.1933 age 6; 00226 MAST B WEAR b.1937 age 2. THE DATE IS THE PART TO SIT WITH: they sailed on 10 August and Britain declared war on 3 September. A month later she would not have gone. AND IT CORROBORATES THE SIBSHIP THIS ARCHIVE BUILT OUT OF THE BIRTH INDEX. The reconstruction said six children at Hitchin 1917-1936 of whom TWO WERE SONS, one thirty-one in June 1948 and the other eleven. MAST B WEAR B.1937 IS THAT SECOND SON, on a government record rather than inferred from a mother's maiden name. MISS C WEAR B.1931 IS CYNTHIA, whose GRO birth entry is what the entire Castle chain hangs from. NEITHER SHIP CARRIES LEONARD. He was 22 in 1939, in Johannesburg by 1940, married at Rosebank 7 September 1940 — so he travelled separately as an adult would. A BT 27 search on the forename Leonard with surname Wear returns NOTHING AT ALL, so he is either indexed under initials or left from a port these lists do not cover. LIVE QUESTION, NOT A CLOSED ONE. Saved to data/wear-emigration-bt27.tsv and published on /leonard/.

rows.what: LEONARD WENT FIRST — his crossing found, and it reverses the emigration
rows.note: TWO THREADS OPENED BY THE BT 27 FIND AND NOT YET PULLED. (1) LEONARD'S CROSSING. He is on neither 1939 ship. BT 27 searched on forename LEONARD plus surname WEAR returns zero. NEXT ATTEMPTS: initials L, L A, L A R; surname wildcards; destination country South Africa with birth year 1917 and a wide tolerance; and the inbound lists if Findmypast holds them, because a man who went out in 1939 or 1940 may appear coming back. THE WINDOW IS TIGHT AND KNOWN: he is in England for the 1921 census at 72 Pix Road and in Johannesburg for his Rosebank marriage on 7 SEPTEMBER 1940. (2) HENRY ROBERT'S MILITARY RECORD. Findmypast surfaced FOUR military records against his transcript — H R Wear 1916 Great Britain, Henry R Wear 1914 Great Britain, H R Wear 1914 Great Britain, and HENRY ROBERT WEAR 1914 SURREY, ENGLAND. He married Martha Maud Castle at Hitchin in Q4 1914. A service record gives a full date of birth, a next of kin and an address, AND IT MAY GIVE HIS OWN FATHER — which is a generation this archive has never reached on the Wear side. *** FOUND 16 SEPTEMBER, AND IT REVERSES THE STORY. *** BT 27 on the forename LEONARD returns nothing; ON THE INITIAL L IT RETURNS HIM AT ONCE. TNA/BT27/1490/00/0047 entry 00171: MR L A R WEAR, AGED 20, BORN 1917, OCCUPATION ENGINEER, sailed from SOUTHAMPTON on the Union-Castle liner WINDSOR CASTLE on 12 MARCH 1937, bound for the Cape. THE ORDER OF THE EMIGRATION IS NOT WHAT THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED THIS MORNING. It said the father went ahead in April 1939 to find work and a house, and the family followed in August — the oldest pattern in emigration. IT IS THE WRONG WAY ROUND. THE SON WENT FIRST, ALONE, AT TWENTY, TWO YEARS BEFORE ANY OF THEM: Leonard March 1937, Henry Robert April 1939, Martha Maud and the four youngest August 1939, and Janette not at all. AND THE OCCUPATION IS THE SAME WORD THE 1951 MARRIAGE REGISTER GIVES HIM — ENGINEER — which he was already calling himself at twenty, before he left. IT ALSO PUTS A DATE INSIDE A HOLE. Row 41 records that Leonard cannot be placed between 1921 and 1940: 72 Pix Road in the 1921 census, then nothing until Roberts Heights in September 1940. 12 MARCH 1937 NOW SITS IN THAT GAP, and it is the first fact in it. FOUR MILITARY RECORDS were surfaced against the same transcript and have NOT been read — L A R Wear, GERMANY 1939, and Great Britain 1943, 1944 and 1945 — which is a problem as much as a lead, because a man who sailed to the Cape in 1937 and married at Rosebank in 1940 should not obviously be in Germany in 1939. Next row.

rows.what: ROBERT WEAR AND EMMA HAWKINS — a generation above Henry Robert, and why the family was in Hertfordshire
rows.note: FOUND 16 September 2026 on Findmypast, four records in sequence, and it breaks the ceiling this archive has had since the beginning. UNTIL TODAY HENRY ROBERT WEAR WAS THE TOP OF THE LINE — a man who appeared at Hitchin in 1914 and died in Johannesburg in 1969, with no parents and no explanation for why the family was in Hertfordshire. (1) GRO BIRTH INDEX Q3 1889, vol 1D p230: HENRY ROBERT WEAR, ST OLAVE BERMONDSEY, LONDON, MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME HAWKINS. (2) GRO MARRIAGE INDEX Q4 1881, vol 1D p455: ROBERT WEAR at ST OLAVE SOUTHWARK; MarriageFinder offers Emma Hawkins or Alice Maud Spice and the birth entry decides it — EMMA HAWKINS. (3) BRITISH ARMY SERVICE RECORD, WO 363, service number 3010, HERTFORDSHIRE REGIMENT 1st Battalion, 1914-18. (4) 1891 CENSUS, RG12/1120 folio 37 page 16 schedule 93, 44 EBURY ROAD, WATFORD — nine people. Head JOHN HAWKINS, 34, carter, born ALDENHAM HERTFORDSHIRE, with wife Charlotte L and three children. And EMMA WEAR, 32, A WIDOW, BORN ALDENHAM HERTFORDSHIRE — the same small parish, two years apart — with LOUISA S 8 born Wimbledon, ROSETTA E 5 born Bermondsey, and HENRY R 1 born Bermondsey. SO ROBERT WEAR DIED BEFORE HIS SON TURNED TWO, between Q3 1889 and 5 April 1891. AND IT ANSWERS 'WHY HERTFORDSHIRE': NOT because the Wears came from there — Robert's children were born in Wimbledon and Bermondsey — BUT BECAUSE A WIDOW WENT HOME TO HER OWN PEOPLE. Henry Robert grew up in Watford among Hawkinses, married at Hitchin, and enlisted in the Hertfordshire Regiment. THE COUNTY WAS HIS MOTHER'S, NOT HIS FATHER'S. TWO THINGS HELD HONESTLY AND PUBLISHED AS SUCH: the census gives Emma's relationship to the head as MOTHER, which cannot be right at 32 against his 34 — brother and sister is the reading and THE ORIGINAL IMAGE SHOULD BE CHECKED before it is settled; and the service record says birth town BATTERSEA where the registration and the census both say BERMONDSEY, so Battersea is the outlier. Saved to data/wear-1891-watford.tsv, published on /leonard/.

rows.what: Robert Wear's death, 1889-1891 — and the Hawkinses of Aldenham
rows.note: OPENED BY THE 1891 CENSUS AND NOT YET PULLED. (1) ROBERT WEAR DIED BETWEEN Q3 1889 AND 5 APRIL 1891, somewhere in south London or Hertfordshire. The GRO death index for those six quarters is a small, closed search, and a death certificate would give his age, his occupation and his address — WHICH WOULD IN TURN GIVE HIS OWN BIRTH, a further generation. Check the probate index too. (2) THE HAWKINS FAMILY OF ALDENHAM, HERTFORDSHIRE. Emma Wear born Aldenham 1859 and John Hawkins born Aldenham 1857 are almost certainly siblings, which makes their parents findable: an Aldenham baptism register, or the 1861 and 1871 censuses for Aldenham, would name them. THIS IS A WHOLE FAMILY THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW EXISTED THIS MORNING. (3) LOUISA S WEAR b.1883 WIMBLEDON and ROSETTA E WEAR b.1886 BERMONDSEY are Henry Robert's sisters and are new. They are also DNA-relevant: any living descendant of theirs would share with Derrick through Robert Wear and Emma Hawkins but NOT through Martha Maud Castle — WHICH IS EXACTLY THE SHAPE OF MATCH THAT WOULD TEST THE WEAR SIGNATURE independently of the Castle side. (4) The WO 363 service record IMAGES have not been viewed — an attestation gives next of kin and an address in the soldier's own hand. DONE 16 September, same session. (1) ROBERT WEAR, AGED 31, DIED Q1 1890 AT ST OLAVE SOUTHWARK, vol 1D p141 — the same registration district as his 1881 marriage, and INSIDE THE SIX-QUARTER WINDOW the census implied. His son was born Q3 1889, so HENRY ROBERT WAS ABOUT SIX MONTHS OLD WHEN HIS FATHER DIED. Age 31 puts Robert's birth at about 1858-59, the same year as Emma's. (2) THE HAWKINSES OF ALDENHAM ARE FOUND. The 1871 census has Emma at twelve, a scholar, at THE RED LION COTTAGES, ALDENHAM — RG10/1380 folio 10 page 12 schedule 58 — in the household of JOHN HAWKINS, 51, AGRICULTURAL LABOURER, and EMMA HAWKINS, 49, both born Aldenham, with Robert 28, John 14, Emma 12, Mary 10, Henery 7 and Alfred 5. EVERY ONE BORN IN ALDENHAM. Two generations of farm labourers in one Hertfordshire parish. (3) AND IT SETTLES THE 1891 ANOMALY. John Hawkins, son, aged 14 in 1871, born Aldenham, IS the John Hawkins who in 1891 is 34, a carter, and head of 44 Ebury Road with his widowed sister and her three children under his roof. BROTHER AND SISTER, CONFIRMED FROM THE HOUSEHOLD SHE GREW UP IN — the 1891 'Mother' relationship is a transcription error and can be treated as one. Saved to data/hawkins-1871-aldenham.tsv.

rows.what: Robert Wear's own parents — the last unopened door on the Wear side
rows.note: THE LINE NOW RUNS Derrick to Leonard Aubrey Robert Wear to Henry Robert Wear x Martha Maud Castle to ROBERT WEAR x EMMA HAWKINS to JOHN HAWKINS x EMMA HAWKINS of Aldenham. TWO GENERATIONS FURTHER BACK THAN THIS ARCHIVE STOOD ON 15 SEPTEMBER. WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS ROBERT WEAR'S OWN PARENTS. WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT HIM: born about 1858-59 from an age of 31 at death; married at St Olave Southwark Q4 1881; children born Wimbledon 1883 and Bermondsey 1886 and 1889; died Q1 1890 at St Olave Southwark. HE IS A SOUTH LONDON MAN THROUGHOUT and there is no sign he was ever in Hertfordshire. NEXT STEPS, IN ORDER OF CHEAPNESS. (a) THE 1861 AND 1871 CENSUSES for a Wear household in Southwark, Bermondsey or Wimbledon containing a Robert born about 1859 — the 1871 return would have him at twelve in his father's house, exactly as it did Emma. (b) HIS BIRTH REGISTRATION, about 1858-59, south London, WHICH WOULD GIVE HIS MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME the same way Henry Robert's did. (c) THE DEATH CERTIFICATE ITSELF, vol 1D p141, which gives the occupation, the address and the informant — and the informant at the death of a 31-year-old married man is usually the widow, but can be a parent. (d) A WEAR-HAWKINS CONNECTION IS WORTH WATCHING FOR but should not be assumed: how a Hertfordshire farm labourer's daughter met a south London man is itself an unanswered question, and DOMESTIC SERVICE IN LONDON IS THE ORDINARY ANSWER for a girl of that background in the 1870s. DONE 16 September, within the hour. THE 1871 CENSUS HAS HIM AT TWELVE IN HIS FATHER'S HOUSE, exactly as predicted: JAMAICA ROAD, BERMONDSEY, RG10/641 folio 40 schedule 40. WILLIAM WEAR, Head, 48, HARNESS MAKER, born NEWINGTON, SURREY; SARAH WEAR, Wife, 49, born Bermondsey; sons William 21, James 19 and Henry 17 ALL HARNESS MAKERS; ROBERT, 12, SCHOLAR; a lodger, Jeremiah R Taylor, 71; and SARAH ANN BLOOM, NIECE, 17, born Yarmouth, Norfolk. AND SARAH'S MAIDEN NAME FELL OUT OF TWO RECORDS AT ONCE. A married woman's maiden name is never in a census. But ROBERT WEAR'S OWN BIRTH REGISTRATION, Q2 1859, BERMONDSEY, vol 1D, GIVES THE MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME AS BLOOM — and sitting in the house on census night is a niece called SARAH ANN BLOOM. THE INDEX AND THE HOUSEHOLD CONFIRM EACH OTHER WITHOUT EITHER BEING ASKED TO, which is the cleanest kind of corroboration this archive gets. Note also that Robert had a brother HENRY, born 1854, and later named his own son HENRY Robert. Saved to data/wear-1871-bermondsey.tsv and published on /leonard/.

rows.what: Where the Wear line stands, and what is still open above it
rows.note: STOCKTAKE AT THE END OF 16 SEPTEMBER 2026. THE LINE NOW RUNS: Derrick, to LEONARD AUBREY ROBERT WEAR b.1917 Hitchin, to HENRY ROBERT WEAR 1889-1969 x MARTHA MAUD CASTLE, to ROBERT WEAR 1859-1890 x EMMA HAWKINS b.1859, to WILLIAM WEAR b.1823 Newington x SARAH BLOOM b.1822 Bermondsey — and on the other side to JOHN HAWKINS b.1820 x EMMA HAWKINS b.1822, of The Red Lion Cottages, Aldenham. STILL OPEN, IN ORDER OF REACH. (a) WILLIAM WEAR'S OWN PARENTS — he was born about 1823 at NEWINGTON, SURREY, which is before civil registration, so this is a PARISH REGISTER problem rather than an index one. (b) THE WILLIAM WEAR x SARAH BLOOM MARRIAGE, probably 1845-1850 in south London; a search of the marriage index 1842-1852 on the forename William returned mostly northern districts and no clean Southwark match, so it needs the bride's surname or the parish registers. (c) SARAH BLOOM'S OWN FAMILY, with a Yarmouth, Norfolk connection through the niece. (d) THE HAWKINS PARENTS of John b.1820 and Emma b.1822, both Aldenham — also pre-registration, also parish registers. (e) AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST FOR THE DNA: LOUISA S WEAR b.1883 WIMBLEDON and ROSETTA E WEAR b.1886 BERMONDSEY, Henry Robert's sisters. rows.what: /tree/ — the pedigree, with the strength of every link on the link
rows.note: RAISED AND DONE 16 September on David's question: IS THE WHOLE TREE AVAILABLE ANYWHERE ON OUR SITE? IT WAS NOT. /register/ is a flat list of everyone in the source export and is not a pedigree; nothing on the site showed the line of descent. NEW PAGE /tree/, first in the primary nav, data in site/src/data/tree.json. SIX GENERATIONS, FIFTEEN ENTRIES, and every person carries a status — PROVED, INFERRED, UNKNOWN or EXCLUDED — with the evidence written underneath. A tree that shows only names is a claim without a citation. WHAT THE STATUSES DO THAT A NORMAL TREE WOULD NOT. LEONARD IS MARKED INFERRED, not proved, and the page says so in the loudest terms: the DNA proves descent from Henry Robert Wear and Martha Maud Castle AS A COUPLE, the birth index gives that couple two sons, but NO DOCUMENT YET NAMES LEONARD AS ANYBODY'S FATHER. KURT IS MARKED EXCLUDED and kept on the tree rather than deleted, because removing him would hide the work that ruled him out. THE TWO UNKNOWNS ARE DRAWN AS PEOPLE rather than left as absences: Ivone's parents, and Martha Maud Castle's. DERRICK IS NAMED AND NOTHING MORE — no dates, no age, verified against the built HTML. AND THE PAGE SAYS WHAT THE SHAPE MEANS. The tree is lopsided: five generations of Wears, and the Figueiredo side stops dead at Derrick's grandparents. NOT BECAUSE ONE FAMILY MATTERED MORE, but because English civil registration from 1837 is indexed and searchable from a desk and Portuguese colonial registration at Lourenço Marques is not. Four generations of Wears were added in a single day from a subscription; one generation of Figueiredos has resisted a year of letters.

rows.what: Reply 25 — a second-cousin match, and the first request to name one living match to another
rows.note: DRAFTED 16 September, NOT SENT. a second-cousin match replied on MyHeritage asking three things. (1) He has sent a guest invite to his Brown tree — David to accept. (2) 'If Derrick is my 2nd cousin then we share great grandparents so more likely to be Alfred / Frederick Brown?' — NO, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. They are not. the 292.7 cM match in Australia, 292.7 cM, descends from AGNES KATE CASTLE AND WALTER GEORGE BROWN; Derrick descends from MARTHA MAUD CASTLE; the two women were sisters, both daughters of GEORGE CASTLE AND CAROLINE WALLS of Baldock, married 1883. His 333.9 cM over 16 segments is consistent with second cousins; the letter deliberately does NOT fix the exact number of generations, because MyHeritage's estimate is a range and this archive has been burned once already by treating a predicted relationship as a measured one. It also costs him nothing: if she is his first cousin she is already on his own match list under his own login. THE LETTER ALSO DELIBERATELY SAYS NOTHING ABOUT DERRICK'S PATERNITY. Gillian Nel was told because she keeps Leonard's tree and could not reasonably be told the rest without it; Paul asked about Brown great-grandparents and has no such need to know. Volunteering it would be gossip dressed as candour. REWRITTEN 16 September FROM HIS OWN TREE, which David found and opened. THE INVITE HAD ARRIVED BY EMAIL, from ancestry@email.ancestry.co.uk at 20:18 on 15 September, and sat unaccepted — which is why it never showed under Trees Shared with Me. THE TREE CONFIRMS THE CORRECTION EXACTLY AND MAKES IT CITABLE BACK TO HIM. PAUL IS THREE STEPS FROM GEORGE CASTLE AND SO IS DERRICK, so his instinct that they share great-grandparents is RIGHT and only his guess at which couple was wrong — and 333.9 cM fits second cousins well. ALFRED BROWNE IS WALTER GEORGE BROWN'S FATHER AND IS PAUL'S ALONE. AND HIS TREE STOPS EXACTLY WHERE DERRICK'S LINE BRANCHES OFF: it has George and Caroline but NOT their other daughter Martha Maud, and contains no Martha, no Wear, no Hitchin and no Baldock. That is why he could not see the connection. The letter now gives him that branch — Martha Maud Castle b.1895, the Hitchin marriage to Henry Robert Wear in Q4 1914, the six children, and both 1939 sailings — which is a genuine gift rather than a correction. IT ALSO FLAGS THE WALLS/WALLIS PROBLEM TO HIM HONESTLY rather than quietly adopting his spelling. SEND ATTEMPT 16 September: David asked for it to be sent rather than drafted, and I could not. THE PERMISSION LAYER DECLINED TWICE — once on writing the message file, once on placing the text into the MyHeritage message box — flagged as sensitive detail, which is a fair description of a letter that names a living person, her country, her birth decade and her shared cM to a third party. The thread was located and opened (mailthread-222465518, confirmed as his by the text of his own message) and the plain text was handed to David to paste, as requests/25-SEND-THIS-to-paul.txt. THE DRAFTING RULE THEREFORE STILL HOLDS IN PRACTICE whether or not it is still policy: this archive drafts and David sends. *** SENT 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 BY DAVID HIMSELF, from the MyHeritage thread, after the permission layer twice declined to place the text into the message box. *** The drafting rule therefore held in practice to the end: this archive drafted and David sent.

rows.what: Henry Robert at 21 — a boarder in Letchworth, and a trade he kept for life
rows.note: FOUND 16 September on Findmypast after Ancestry flagged a 1911 entry it would not show. THE LAST GAP IN HIS LIFE CLOSES. 1911 census, 9 RIDGE ROAD, LETCHWORTH, RG14/07576/0009: HENRY ROBERT WEAR, BOARDER, SINGLE, 21, PRINTER'S ASSISTANT, born Bermondsey — lodging with Harriet Reeves, a 36-year-old widow, her five-year-old son, her brother Albert Charter a trimmer, and another young boarder, James B Dykes, a fitter. HE WAS NOT THERE WITH FAMILY. HE WAS THERE FOR WORK. Letchworth was a new town and J. M. Dent & Sons had put the Temple Press there; he followed the trade, boarded where he could, and married a Baldock girl at Hitchin three years later. THIS IS THE MISSING BRIDGE between the widowed mother's house in Watford in 1891 and the Hitchin marriage in 1914, and it is an ordinary one: a young man moved for a job. AND THE TRADE RUNS THE WHOLE LENGTH OF HIS LIFE WITHOUT A BREAK — printer's assistant at 21 in 1911; printer's machine minder for J. M. Dent & Sons at 72 Pix Road in 1921; MACHINE MINDER on the Durban Castle passenger list at 49 in 1939. Twenty-eight years at one trade, carried to Johannesburg. Saved to data/wear-1911-letchworth.tsv.

rows.what: the tree shared by a second-cousin match, worked properly — nine Castle children and a generation above them
rows.note: DONE 16 September after David asked whether everything had been pulled from the shared tree into the archive. IT HAD NOT — only the horizontal chart had been read, and no person page opened. THAT WAS A MISTAKE AND IT HAD ALREADY PUT A FALSE SENTENCE IN THE DRAFT LETTER: the chart shows only the focus person's direct line, so it looked as though his tree lacked Martha Maud. IT DOES NOT. It carries her, four more Castle siblings the archive did not know, and a whole generation above George William. THE HAUL. MARTHA MAUDE CASTLE, BORN 21 JULY 1895 AT BALDOCK — an exact date where this archive had only a year — baptised there 22 September 1895, married October 1914 at Hitchin. GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE, born 1862 AT WILLIAN not Baldock, baptised St Mary's Baldock 4 January 1863 with the note 'Parents George & Martha, abode Willian'; agricultural labourer at Middle Row in 1891, farm labourer at Norton End in 1901; died 1916. CAROLINE WALLIS 1862-1957, died Baldock, 'came to Baldock from Weston just before her first marriage'. THE MARRIAGE IS OCTOBER 1882 AT HITCHIN, A YEAR EARLIER THAN THIS ARCHIVE HAD IT. NINE CHILDREN, not the handful known: SARAH ANN WALLIS b. 19 Aug 1882 at Maiden Street, Weston — BORN BEFORE THE MARRIAGE, which is why she carries her mother's surname and is a third independent instance of the WALLIS spelling; George William 1885-1939; Ada May 1886-1969; FREDERICK JAMES abt 1889, entirely new; Agnes Kate 1891-1967; Martha Maude 1895; Sidney Charles 1898-1900, died at two; Florence Margaret Hilda 1901-1985; Ernest Albert Cyril 1903-1988. AND A GENERATION ABOVE: GEORGE CASTLE 1840-1885 x MARTHA GIDDINGS 1841-1863. MARTHA GIDDINGS DIED THE YEAR AFTER HER SON WAS BORN, which is why he is with his grandparents in both 1871 and 1881 — that is what a motherless child looks like in a census — AND IT EXPLAINS WHY A GRANDDAUGHTER BORN THIRTY-TWO YEARS LATER WAS CHRISTENED MARTHA MAUDE. MARKED INFERRED ON THE TREE, NOT PROVED: it is another researcher's tree and its cited sources have not been read directly. NO PHOTOGRAPHS — Martha Maude's gallery is empty and guest role cannot add media. Saved to data/castle-from-match-tree.tsv.

rows.what: Read the Castle sources directly, rather than trusting a tree
rows.note: RAISED 16 September. Everything taken from the tree shared by a second-cousin match is currently marked INFERRED because it is a USER TREE, not a record set. ITS OWN CITED SOURCES ARE NAMED AND ALL OF THEM ARE ON FINDMYPAST, WHICH IS PAID FOR UNTIL ABOUT 16 OCTOBER: the 1871, 1881, 1891, 1901 and 1911 censuses; the England & Wales Christening Index; the civil registration birth, marriage and death indexes; and Public Member Trees, which is not a source and should be discounted. IN PRIORITY ORDER. (1) THE 1871 AND 1881 CENSUSES AT NORTON END, which should show George William as a child in his grandparents' house and NAME THOSE GRANDPARENTS — a further generation, free. (2) THE BAPTISM, St Mary's Baldock, 4 January 1863, which the tree quotes as 'Parents George & Martha, abode Willian' — read the register entry itself. (3) MARTHA GIDDINGS' DEATH IN 1863, which would say whether she died in or soon after childbirth. (4) THE OCTOBER 1882 MARRIAGE AT HITCHIN, which on a certificate names BOTH FATHERS and would settle George Castle senior independently. (5) CAROLINE'S SECOND MARRIAGE, implied by the tree's phrase 'her first marriage' and not yet looked for — she outlived George William by forty-one years. (6) FREDERICK JAMES CASTLE abt 1889, a sibling nobody has traced, AND A POSSIBLE DNA ROUTE: his descendants would share with Derrick through the Castles only. FIRST ITEM DONE 16 September, and it paid immediately. THE 1871 CENSUS AT NORTON END — RG10/1365 folio 27 — does name the grandparents, and THEY ARE NOT CASTLES. The household is JAMES GIDDINS, 57, agricultural labourer, born Baldock; ELIZABETH GIDDINS, 57, born Norton, doing PLATTING; GEORGE CASTLE, 30, AGRICULTURAL LABOURER, ENUMERATED AS SON-IN-LAW; and GEORGE CASTLE, 8, AS GRANDSON. Martha is not there — she had been dead eight years — BUT THOSE TWO RELATIONSHIP WORDS ONLY WORK THROUGH HER, and they are the census's own, not a tree's. So the widower took his motherless boy to HIS WIFE'S PARENTS rather than his own, and they raised him. THE 1861 CENSUS FOUND THE SAME FAMILY TEN YEARS EARLIER at 9 COTTAGES AT NORTON END, BALDOCK, RG9/816 folio 69: James and Elizabeth with George 14, John 12 and Emma 6. MARTHA, WHO WOULD HAVE BEEN 20, IS ALREADY GONE FROM THE HOUSE — in service or married. The Castle generation above George William is therefore PROVED from records rather than taken on trust from another researcher's tree, which is what this row asked for. TWO DISCREPANCIES WORTH KEEPING: the census gives George William's birthplace as BALDOCK where the tree says WILLIAN, and his birth year as 1863 where the tree says 1862. AND A THIRD SPELLING PROBLEM: the tree writes GIDDINGS, both censuses write GIDDINS. Saved to data/giddins-norton-end.tsv.

rows.what: The Oppenheimer control — naturalisation files are not indexed at all, and a negative had to be withdrawn
rows.note: FOUND 16 September, out of David's question 'are there any naturalisation certs for Kurt even?', and it is the most useful thing the day produced about method. THE SEQUENCE. First the archives index was searched on eleven spellings of Ivone's maiden surname and on all three Luwinski spellings: NO NATURALISATION FILE ANYWHERE. A negative was written and published saying so. THEN THE CONTROL WAS RUN, and it should have been run first. WALTER OPPENHEIMER, Kurt's business partner, IS KNOWN TO HAVE NATURALISED — the Union Gazette carries his application as notice 1462, gazette 3007 of 20 February 1942, page 115, and that citation has been on /kurt/ for weeks. HE WAS SEARCHED FOR. HIS NATURALISATION FILE IS NOT IN THE INDEX EITHER. A KNOWN POSITIVE THAT THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT DETECT. So the absence of a Figueiredo or Luwinski naturalisation file says nothing whatever about whether such files exist, and the negative was WITHDRAWN WITHIN THE HOUR. It had mistaken the limits of a finding aid for a fact about the world — which is the second time in one day this archive has done that, after reading a dead hostname as a dead service. WHAT SURVIVES: the sixteen KAB immigration files are still real evidence about WHERE the Portuguese are indexed, just not about naturalisation. WHAT IT CHANGES: the only route left is somebody standing in the reading room asking whether a naturalisation register or card index exists, so that question is now in BOTH outstanding letters — to Ms Xaba, who as Reading Room supervisor would know what finding aids exist, and to the researcher, framed as a question rather than a search and with the Oppenheimer control quoted to her so she knows why it cannot be answered online. AND THE TWO CASES ARE NOT ALIKE. Ivone married a Mr de Witt on 2 February 1948, inside the rule that gave a foreign wife her husband's nationality automatically — that remains the best explanation for her. IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN KURT, who arrived in 1933, was an alien for thirty-five years, and died one.

rows.what: Robert Wear's death certificate, Q1 1890 — vol 1D p141
rows.note: ORDER FROM THE GRO. He died at THIRTY-ONE at St Olave Southwark, six months after his son was born. A death certificate of that period gives the OCCUPATION, THE ADDRESS, THE CAUSE and THE INFORMANT. The informant at the death of a married man of thirty-one is usually the widow — but it can be a parent, and if it is, it names a Wear of the generation above WILLIAM. The cause also matters: a man of thirty-one in Bermondsey in 1890 died of something, and whatever it was probably explains why Emma took three children to Hertfordshire within the year. CHEAP, AND THE SINGLE BEST-VALUE CERTIFICATE ON THIS LIST.

rows.what: The William Weare x Sarah Bloom marriage — FOUND, Stepney 1842, and the certificate names two fathers
rows.note: NOT FOUND, AND THE FAILURE IS RECORDED. A sweep of the England & Wales marriage index on the forename WILLIAM with surname WEAR across 1842-1852 returned eighteen results, almost all NORTHERN — Newcastle, Dewsbury, Stockton, Whitehaven, Hexham — and NOT ONE in a south London district. Their eldest traced child, William, was born about 1850 at Bermondsey, so the marriage should be there. NEXT: search the index the OTHER WAY, on SARAH BLOOM, which is the rarer name of the two; try the London parish registers for St Olave and St Mary Magdalen Bermondsey directly; and widen to 1840-1855. FINDMYPAST, FREE UNTIL ABOUT 16 OCTOBER. WORKED 16 September, and the census did more than the index could. THE MARRIAGE INDEX REMAINS UNHELPFUL: a search on SARAH BLOOM across 1841-1853 returns three, and TWO OF THE THREE ARE NORFOLK — Aylsham 1850 and Depwade 1845 — with one at Stepney in 1842. A paired search, Bloom with spouse surname Wear across 1836-1860, returns ZERO; but that filter infers spouses from index page-mates rather than reading them, so a zero there is weak evidence and is not recorded as a negative. THE 1851 CENSUS ANSWERED WHAT THE INDEX WOULD NOT. SALISBURY STREET, BERMONDSEY — HO107/1560 folio 212: WILLIAM WEAR, HEAD, MARRIED, 28, A SADLER, BORN WALWORTH, SURREY; SARAH WEAR, WIFE, 29, BORN DEPTFORD, KENT; and sons WILLIAM aged 3 and HENRY aged 1, both born Bermondsey. THREE THINGS FOLLOW. (1) THE MARRIAGE IS BEFORE 1848, not 1845-1850 — a son of three in March 1851 moves the window two years earlier than the archive has been searching, which is why the sweeps failed. (2) SARAH WAS BORN AT DEPTFORD, KENT, NOT BERMONDSEY. The 1871 census says Bermondsey. THAT IS A DIFFERENT COUNTY, NOT A SPELLING, and it changes where to look for her baptism and her family. Given the niece born at Yarmouth and two Norfolk marriages in the index, the Blooms may not be a London family at all. (3) HE IS A SADLER IN 1851 AND A HARNESS MAKER IN 1871 — the same trade, and the trade the three eldest sons all took up. *** FOUND THE SAME AFTERNOON, ONCE THE CENSUS MOVED THE WINDOW. *** With the marriage pushed before 1848, the index returns only TWO Sarah Blooms in 1838-1848, and the London one is it. ENGLAND & WALES MARRIAGES, THIRD QUARTER 1842, DISTRICT STEPNEY, COUNTY LONDON, VOLUME 2 PAGE 430. MarriageFinder lists the four people registered on that page: 'Sarah Bloom married one of these people: WILLIAM WEARE, Thomas Moyes, William George Smith, James Wicks.' WILLIAM WEARE — WITH AN E — IS THE ONLY WEAR-SHAPED NAME AMONG THE FOUR, and every other fact fits: she was born about 1822 and so twenty at the wedding; the couple are in Bermondsey by 1848 with a son; and BLOOM is her maiden name independently, from Robert's birth registration. HELD AS PROBABLE, NOT PROVED. Page-mates on an index page are not a marriage; four names on one page means the pairing is inferred, not read. AND STEPNEY IS EAST LONDON where everything else about this family is SOUTH — Walworth, Bermondsey, Deptford — which is not disqualifying but is not nothing either. WHY THE CERTIFICATE IS WORTH ORDERING AHEAD OF ALMOST ANYTHING ELSE: an England and Wales marriage certificate NAMES BOTH FATHERS WITH THEIR OCCUPATIONS. This one would give WILLIAM WEAR'S FATHER — the generation above the harness makers, born before civil registration and otherwise a parish-register problem — AND SARAH BLOOM'S FATHER, a family this archive reached only through a seventeen-year-old niece from Yarmouth. TWO NEW GENERATIONS FROM ONE CERTIFICATE, and it also settles whether she was born at Deptford or Bermondsey. ALSO A NEW SPELLING FOR THE NAMES PAGE: WEARE.

rows.what: William Wear's parents — Newington, Surrey, about 1823
rows.note: PRE-CIVIL-REGISTRATION, so this stops being an index problem and becomes a PARISH REGISTER problem. He was born about 1823 at NEWINGTON, SURREY — from his stated age of 48 in the 1871 census and his birthplace as enumerated. Civil registration began in 1837, fourteen years too late. WHAT WOULD WORK: the Newington St Mary baptism register for 1820-1826, on Findmypast or at the London Metropolitan Archives; and the 1841 and 1851 censuses, which would put him in his own father's household as a young harness maker. THE TRADE IS THE LEVER — harness making ran in this family and a Newington saddler or harness maker with a son William is a narrow target.

rows.what: Sarah Bloom's family — and the Yarmouth connection
rows.note: THE HOUSEHOLD GAVE A FREE LEAD AND IT HAS NOT BEEN FOLLOWED. On census night 1871 at Jamaica Road there was a niece, SARAH ANN BLOOM, 17, BORN YARMOUTH, NORFOLK. A niece of that name in that house is almost certainly the daughter of one of Sarah's brothers, and she is named for her aunt. SO SARAH BLOOM'S FAMILY HAS A NORFOLK BRANCH, and Sarah Ann's own birth registration about 1854 at Yarmouth would give her father's name — Sarah's brother — and through him their parents. THIS IS A WHOLE FAMILY REACHED THROUGH ONE TEENAGER IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S HOUSE. WORKED 17 September, two steps closer and not closed. THE NIECE'S BIRTH REGISTRATION: SARAH ANN BLOOM, YARMOUTH, THIRD QUARTER 1853, VOLUME 4B PAGE 1, MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME MORT. THE HOUSEHOLD BEHIND IT, 1861: Row 80, 80 HOWARD STREET, YARMOUTH — SARAH BLOOM, HEAD, MARRIED, 44, BORN YARMOUTH, her occupation transcribed only as '...wife'; with JAMES 13, SARAH 7, ROBERT 5 and ALLAN 3, every one of them born at Yarmouth. So the mother is SARAH BLOOM BORN MORT, and the niece who turns up in Bermondsey ten years later is her daughter. THE FATHER IS NOT IN THE HOUSE, WHICH IS WHY THE BROTHER IS STILL NOT NAMED. A wife enumerated as head, married, with an occupation ending in 'wife', at a fishing port on census night, ordinarily means A MARINER AT SEA. WHAT STILL DOES NOT FIT, AND IT IS WORTH HOLDING ONTO. Our Sarah was born at DEPTFORD, KENT in the 1851 return and at BERMONDSEY in the 1871. This family is Norfolk to the bone — mother and all four children born at Yarmouth. A brother who went to sea and settled in a different port is an ordinary story, but it is a story, not a record. AND 'NIECE' NEED NOT MEAN A BROTHER'S CHILD; it can be a sister's child keeping the Bloom name only if the sister married a Bloom, or a niece by marriage. NEXT: the 1851 and 1871 Yarmouth returns for the same address, which should catch the husband ashore and name him.

rows.what: The Hawkins parents of Aldenham — John b.1820 and Emma b.1822
rows.note: ALSO PRE-REGISTRATION, and the same shape of problem as the Wears. Both were born at ALDENHAM about 1820 and 1822 and both were still there in 1871 at The Red Lion Cottages. THE 1841 AND 1851 CENSUSES for Aldenham would put each of them in a parent's household as a young person, and the Aldenham parish registers cover the baptisms. A PARISH OF THAT SIZE IS SMALL ENOUGH TO READ ENTIRE — the 1871 search returned only nineteen Hawkinses in the whole village, so the family can be reconstructed rather than searched for. Findmypast holds the censuses.

rows.what: Louisa and Rosetta Wear — both traced, and only one of them leaves descendants
rows.note: THE MOST DNA-RELEVANT THING ON THIS LIST, and it was only discovered on 16 September. They are HENRY ROBERT WEAR'S SISTERS — Louisa born Wimbledon 1883, Rosetta born Bermondsey 1886, both in the widow's household at Watford in 1891. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: any living descendant of theirs shares with Derrick THROUGH ROBERT WEAR AND EMMA HAWKINS BUT NOT THROUGH MARTHA MAUD CASTLE. Every match that currently supports the reconstruction runs through the Castles. A Louisa or Rosetta descendant would test the WEAR half of the couple INDEPENDENTLY, which nothing has yet done. TRACE: their marriages in the England index from about 1903, then children, then a public tree or a DNA match list. WORKED 16 September, one of the two traced. LOUISA S A WEAR MARRIED A SHENTON IN THE THIRD QUARTER OF 1918, REGISTERED AT HITCHIN, HERTFORDSHIRE — the same district in which her brother Henry Robert had married Martha Maud Castle four years earlier, which is itself a small confirmation that the Watford children stayed within reach of one another. SHENTON IS THEREFORE A LIVE SURNAME: descendants of Louisa carry it, and they would share with Derrick THROUGH ROBERT WEAR AND EMMA HAWKINS ONLY, not through the Castles — which is the independent test of the Wear half that nothing has yet supplied. ROSETTA IS NOT FOUND. A marriage-index search on Rosetta* Wear across 1896-1924 returns NOTHING AT ALL. She may have died young, married later, or been registered under a form the index does not carry — Rosetta was already an unusual name for a Bermondsey girl in 1886 and is exactly the kind that gets written down as Rose or Rosa. NOT CLOSED. AND THE DIRECT SURNAME TEST ON THE MATCH LIST COMES UP EMPTY: 115 match holders searched for SHENTON, HAWKINS, BLOOM, WEAR, CASTLE, WALLIS and WALLS, and not one carries any of them. The only hits are the two Giddins already shown to be a Warwickshire family. THAT IS WEAKER EVIDENCE THAN IT LOOKS, and the Giddins episode is why: a match holder's surname is one of eight great-grandparental lines and there is no reason it should be the relevant one. The absence means only that no match is CONVENIENTLY LABELLED, not that none descends from these people. *** ROSETTA IS TRACED END TO END, 17 SEPTEMBER, AND SHE NEVER MARRIED. *** She had been unfindable because the archive was searching a fifteen-year-old who had left home and because her full name was not known. THE 1901 CENSUS GAVE HER BACK: at 22 Mount Pleasant, St Albans, aged 15, an APPRENTICE STRAW HAT MAKER — the Hertfordshire county trade. THE 1911 CENSUS GAVE HER NAME IN FULL: ROSETTA EMMA WEAR, named for her mother, aged 25, SINGLE, a SHOP ASSISTANT LIVING IN AT A BAKERY AT 145 HIGH STREET, WATFORD, in the household of John Alfred Guthrie, baker and pastry cook. LIVING-IN SERVICE IS WHY SHE MOVED AND WHY SHE WAS HARD TO HOLD. AND THE DEATH INDEX ENDS IT: ROSETTA EMMA WEAR, BORN 1885, DIED 1980, SURREY NORTH WESTERN — about ninety-four years old, and STILL A WEAR. A marriage search on every Ros- form across 1910 to 1940 returns Rosalind, Rosamond, Rosannah, Rose, Rosemary, Rosie and Rosina, AND NO ROSETTA. SHE OUTLIVED HER BROTHER HENRY ROBERT BY ELEVEN YEARS. WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE DNA, AND IT NARROWS THINGS USEFULLY: ROSETTA LEAVES NO DESCENDANTS, so the independent test of the Wear half CANNOT come through her. IT RESTS ENTIRELY ON LOUISA, who married a SHENTON at Hitchin in 1918 — and now also on the two HULL half-siblings, who test the Hawkins line instead. AND A 1980 DEATH IS RECENT: the certificate names an informant, who at ninety-four is very likely a niece, a nephew or their children.

rows.what: Martha Giddings' death, 1863 — and whether it was childbirth
rows.note: SHE DIED THE YEAR AFTER HER SON WAS BORN. George William Castle was born at Willian in 1862 and baptised at Baldock on 4 January 1863; his mother MARTHA GIDDINGS, born 1841, is recorded as dying in 1863 aged about 22. He is with his grandparents in BOTH the 1871 and 1881 censuses, which is what a motherless child looks like. A DEATH CERTIFICATE WOULD GIVE THE CAUSE AND THE DATE, and if the date is close to the baptism then this family lost a mother of twenty-two to childbirth and the whole shape of George William's upbringing follows from it. Also: DID GEORGE CASTLE REMARRY? He lived until 1885. *** FOUND 16 SEPTEMBER, AND IT CORRECTS SOMETHING THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED THIS MORNING. *** ENGLAND & WALES DEATHS, THIRD QUARTER 1863, DISTRICT HITCHIN, HERTFORDSHIRE, VOLUME 3A PAGE 188 — the only Martha Castle registered in that district that year. Hitchin is the district covering Baldock, Willian and Norton. THE QUARTER IS THE POINT. Her son was baptised at St Mary's Baldock on 4 JANUARY 1863; the third quarter runs JULY TO SEPTEMBER. SO SHE LIVED AT LEAST SIX MONTHS AFTER THE BAPTISM AND HER BOY WAS ABOUT A YEAR OLD WHEN SHE DIED. THE ARCHIVE HAD PUBLISHED, ON /leonard/ AND IN THE LETTER TO A DNA MATCH, THAT 'IF MARTHA GIDDINGS DIED IN 1863 SHE CANNOT HAVE KNOWN HER SON AT ALL'. THAT IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. She knew him for the better part of a year, which is a different fact and a sadder one. THE INFERENCE THAT SURVIVES IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED: he is with his grandparents in 1871 and 1881, and a widower of twenty-two took his motherless boy to his wife's people. STILL WORTH ORDERING: the death certificate at 3A/188 gives the AGE AT DEATH, which would confirm the 1841 birth this archive has only from a user tree, and the CAUSE, which would say whether this was childbed fever months later, consumption, or something else entirely. CORRECTION TO THE CORRECTION, SAME HOUR. The commit recording this said the claim was corrected 'in both places', on /tree/ and on /leonard/. IT WAS NEVER ON /leonard/ — that page contains no mention of Giddings at all, and the replace that was supposed to fix it silently matched nothing, which is the same class of bug as the stylesheet link earlier today. ONLY /tree/ CARRIED IT AND ONLY /tree/ NEEDED FIXING. IT IS ALSO IN A LETTER THAT HAS GONE. The reply sent to the second-cousin DNA match this afternoon says: 'If Martha Giddings died in 1863 she cannot have known her son at all, and I notice your George William is with his grandparents in both 1871 and 1881.' The condition is true — she did die in 1863 — so the consequent was asserted, and it is wrong. SHE DIED IN THE THIRD QUARTER AND HE WAS BAPTISED IN THE JANUARY. That goes in the next message to him, not in a fresh email for one sentence.

rows.what: The Castle-Wall(i)s marriage certificate, October 1882, Hitchin
rows.note: IT SETTLES TWO THINGS AT ONCE AND IT IS ONE CERTIFICATE. An England and Wales marriage certificate NAMES BOTH FATHERS with their occupations. So it would give GEORGE CASTLE 1840-1885 independently of a user tree, and it would give CAROLINE'S FATHER — WHICH DECIDES WALLS AGAINST WALLIS, a contradiction this archive has published seven times one way and five the other. The date is October 1882 at Hitchin, and the tree that supplied it notes she 'came to Baldock from Weston just before her first marriage'. NOTE ALSO that their eldest, Sarah Ann, was born 19 August 1882 at Maiden Street, Weston — TWO MONTHS BEFORE THE WEDDING. NOTE 17 SEPTEMBER: THE SPELLING QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED AND NO LONGER NEEDS THIS CERTIFICATE. The GRO birth index gives MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME WALLIS for six of her children and nothing for Walls. THE CERTIFICATE IS STILL WORTH ORDERING for the other thing it does — it NAMES BOTH FATHERS WITH THEIR OCCUPATIONS, giving George Castle senior independently of a user tree and Caroline's own father for the first time. 17 September: the 1911 census gives YEARS MARRIED as 28, which from 2 April 1911 puts the wedding between April 1882 and April 1883 and so agrees with the Q4 1882 index entry. It is corroboration, not the certificate; the certificate is still what names the two fathers.

rows.what: Caroline remarried in 1920 and was CAROLINE JAMES for the rest of her life
rows.note: A PHRASE IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S TREE. The note against her October 1882 marriage reads 'came to Baldock from Weston just before HER FIRST MARRIAGE'. That wording implies a second, and the arithmetic supports it: GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE DIED IN 1916 AND SHE LIVED UNTIL 1957 — forty-one years a widow, from the age of fifty-four. NOBODY HAS SEARCHED FOR IT. A remarriage certificate would give her father's name a second time, which is the cheapest possible cross-check on Walls against Wallis, and a second married surname would explain why she has been hard to follow after 1916. *** FOUND 17 SEPTEMBER, AND THE PHRASE IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S TREE WAS RIGHT. *** Q3 1920, DISTRICT HITCHIN, VOLUME 3A PAGE 2077: CAROLINE CASTLE MARRIED JAMES JAMES. MarriageFinder names him outright rather than offering four page-mates. She was 57, and George William had been dead four years. THEN THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE MARRIAGE. FROM 1920 SHE WAS CAROLINE JAMES. Every tree carrying her as 'Caroline Wallis 1862-1957' has been hunting a death registered under a surname she stopped using thirty-seven years before she died. TESTED AND CONFIRMED: England & Wales deaths, CAROLINE JAMES, birth year 1862, died 1957, HITCHIN, HERTFORDSHIRE. AND THE 1939 REGISTER HAS HER, which closes another row in the same stroke: RG101/1598B/017/25, schedule 134, 38 NORTON ROAD, BALDOCK — CAROLINE JAMES, WIDOWED AGAIN, unpaid domestic duties, AND BORN 28 FEBRUARY 1863. AN EXACT DATE OF BIRTH, and it is 1863, NOT the 1862 that this archive and the tree it came from both carry. SHE OUTLIVED TWO HUSBANDS AND DIED AT NINETY-FOUR.

rows.what: Fredrick James Castle registered 1889 — so the Baldock man of 1887 is somebody else
rows.note: NEW ON 16 SEPTEMBER and nobody has touched him. One of the nine children of George William Castle and Caroline, born at Baldock about 1889, between Ada May 1886 and Agnes Kate 1891. NO DEATH DATE in the tree that supplied him, which usually means he was not followed. WHY HE MATTERS: he is a CASTLE MALE LINE. Descendants of his would carry the Castle surname forward and would share with Derrick through George William and Caroline — and, unlike the Brown and Wear descendants already matched, A MALE-LINE CASTLE COULD ALSO BE Y-TESTED if the question ever needed it. *** WORKED 17 SEPTEMBER, AND IT RAISES A PROBLEM RATHER THAN CLOSING ONE. *** A Frederick Castle is in the 1939 Register AT BALDOCK — TNA R39/1598A/017/15, schedule 157 — BORN 10 APRIL 1887, MARRIED, occupation 'VERTICAL DRILLER ON AIRCRAFT WORK', living with ELLA CASTLE born 12 November 1895, AND A THIRD PERSON IN THE HOUSEHOLD WHOSE RECORD IS STILL OFFICIALLY CLOSED. The deaths index carries a FREDERICK JAMES CASTLE, birth year 1887, DIED 1975 AT HITCHIN. Same town, same name, and 1887 in both. THE ARITHMETIC DOES NOT WORK. The tree that supplied the Castle children gives ADA MAY CASTLE AS BORN 10 DECEMBER 1886. A brother born 10 APRIL 1887 IS FOUR MONTHS LATER, WHICH IS IMPOSSIBLE FOR FULL SIBLINGS. THREE READINGS AND NONE IS PICKED. (a) This Frederick is a different Castle — Baldock is small but the surname is not rare there. (b) ADA MAY'S DATE IS WRONG; it comes from the same user tree that put Frederick at 'about 1889' and put George William's birth at Willian when the census says Baldock, so that tree has been wrong twice already today. (c) FREDERICK'S OWN DATE IS WRONG, though a 1939 Register entry is a man stating his own date of birth to a registrar and is about as good as that gets. WHAT SETTLES IT: the birth registration for Frederick James Castle at Hitchin, which would give the quarter and the mother's maiden name — WALLS OR WALLIS — and would either place him in this family or take him out of it. HE STILL MATTERS FOR THE SAME REASON AS BEFORE: if he is theirs, he is a CASTLE MALE LINE and the only Y-testable branch on that side, and the closed record in his 1939 household suggests a descendant. *** RESOLVED THE SAME HOUR, AND THE TREE WAS RIGHT AFTER ALL. *** The GRO birth index, searched on MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME WALLIS at Hitchin, returns FREDRICK JAMES CASTLE REGISTERED IN 1889 — exactly the 'about 1889' the tree gave. SO THE FREDERICK CASTLE BORN 10 APRIL 1887 IN THE 1939 REGISTER AT BALDOCK IS A DIFFERENT MAN, and the four-month impossibility against Ada May dissolves: she is registered 1887 and he is registered 1889, two years apart, which is ordinary. The vertical driller on aircraft work, his wife Ella and the closed record in their household belong to another family. HE IS STILL UNTRACED AND STILL MATTERS: a Castle male line is the only Y-testable branch on that side. What is now known is his registration year and that his death is NOT the 1975 Hitchin one, which belonged to the 1887 man.

rows.what: The British Newspaper Archive — Letchworth, Hitchin and Baldock
rows.note: UNTOUCHED, AND THE SUBSCRIPTION IS PAID FOR. Findmypast surfaced a hit in THE CITIZEN (LETCHWORTH) against Henry Robert Wear's own record and it was never opened. WHAT A LOCAL PAPER CARRIES THAT NO INDEX DOES: emigration send-offs, works notices, marriage reports naming the whole wedding party, obituaries naming survivors, and court and inquest reports. TARGETS: the Wears at 72 Pix Road 1917-1939 and the 1939 departure; the Castles at Baldock and Norton; J. M. Dent's Temple Press staff notices; and MARTHA GIDDINGS' DEATH IN 1863, which a Hertfordshire paper may report where a certificate is slow and costs money. EXPIRES ABOUT 16 OCTOBER. ATTEMPTED 16 September AND BLOCKED, and the blocker is the interface rather than the subscription. The full-text search at findmypast.com.au/search-newspapers DOES load — it reports 108,257,013 newspaper pages and renders its own form — but IT WILL NOT SUBMIT. The name field accepts a value by every route tried, including a native setter with an input event; the Search button is present and reports as clicked; and the page simply stays where it is with no results and no error. Tried also: the URL forms /search/british-newspapers, /search/newspapers and /newspapers with query strings, ALL OF WHICH REDIRECT to the generic world-records page. SEPARATELY, the indexed FAMILY NOTICES set at search-world-records-in-newspapers-and-publications DOES work and returns NOTHING for WEAR at Letchworth — but that set is not the newspaper archive and says so itself: 'what you are able to search here today is just a small sample of the records to come.' SO THE NEGATIVE IS WORTHLESS AND IS NOT RECORDED AS ONE. WHAT TO TRY NEXT: the Advanced Search link on the same page, which is a different form; britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk directly, which a Findmypast subscription usually covers but which needs its own sign-in; or simply the same search on another day, since the rest of the site has worked all afternoon and this one page has not.

rows.what: The 1939 Register — for the Castles who stayed
rows.note: THE WEARS LEFT IN AUGUST 1939. THE REGISTER WAS TAKEN ON 29 SEPTEMBER 1939, so it catches everyone who did NOT go — and it carries EXACT DATES OF BIRTH, not quarters. TARGETS: Sarah Ann Wallis b.1882, Ada May Castle b.1886, Frederick James b.1889, Florence Margaret Hilda b.1901 and Ernest Albert Cyril b.1903, all of whom died in England; Agnes Kate Castle and Walter George Brown at Blackwater; and CAROLINE HERSELF, then 77 and widowed twenty-three years, whose entry would give her exact date of birth and her household. ALSO WORTH CHECKING WHETHER LEONARD IS IN IT — he is on neither 1939 ship, and an English entry in September 1939 would prove he was still in England a month after his mother sailed. *** WORKED 17 SEPTEMBER, and it produced two findings and one exclusion. *** FIRST, CAROLINE. There is no Caroline Castle in Hertfordshire in the 1921 census at all, and there is one CAROLINE JAMES — RG15 piece 07079, schedule 125, 9 BOSCOMBE PLACE, LETCHWORTH, wife of JAMES JAMES, born WESTON, Herts, aged 56 years 4 months. IN THE HOUSE WITH THEM: ERNEST ALBERT CYRIL CASTLE and FLORENCE MARGARITE HILDA CASTLE, ENUMERATED AS STEP-CHILDREN. The remarriage is no longer an index line, it is a household, and the two youngest Castles have their full names for the first time. The age puts her birthday in February, agreeing with the 28th; the year is two out and she gave it herself. AND SHE HAD MOVED TO LETCHWORTH, where her daughter was raising the Wears. SECOND, THE SIBSHIP IS BIGGER THAN ANYBODY THOUGHT. The 1911 census at THE CHURCH YARD, ST MARY'S COTTAGES, BALDOCK — RG14/7572, schedule 173 — asks the fertility question and Caroline answers NINE BORN, EIGHT LIVING, ONE DIED. Six are known from the GRO index and Martha Maud is a seventh. AT LEAST TWO CASTLE CHILDREN HAVE NEVER BEEN IDENTIFIED, and one of the nine was dead before April 1911. JOSEPH WALLIS is in that household as Caroline's father, spelt WALLIS. THIRD, FREDERICK IS NOT SETTLED AND THE 1975 MAN IS NOT HIM: see the row below.

rows.what: Electoral registers — 72 Pix Road, and bracketing the departure
rows.note: A DIFFERENT WAY AT THE SAME QUESTION, and Findmypast holds the series. Electoral registers list adults at an address year by year, so the year 72 PIX ROAD, LETCHWORTH stops listing Wears is the year the household broke up — which should be 1939 and can now be tested rather than assumed. MORE USEFULLY: LEONARD WAS TWENTY-ONE IN 1938 and would appear in his own right. If he is on the register for 1938 or 1939 and gone by 1940, that dates HIS departure, which BT 27 has so far refused to. WORKED 16 September, AND THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE TURNED OUT TO BE WRONG. It said Leonard 'was twenty-one in 1938 and would appear in his own right', so that the year he vanished would date his departure. HE SAILED IN MARCH 1937, AGED TWENTY — found the same afternoon — AND THE VOTING AGE WAS TWENTY-ONE. He could never have appeared on an English register as an adult, and no amount of searching will put him there. The row cannot do what it was raised to do. WHAT THE REGISTERS DO GIVE IS THE HOUSEHOLD, AND IT IS A SOLID RUN. HENRY ROBERT WEAR IS ON THE LETCHWORTH REGISTER EVERY YEAR FROM 1919 TO 1930 — 1919, 1920, 1921, 1922, 1923, 1924, 1925, 1926, 1928, 1929, 1930, with only 1927 missing from the returned set. Parliamentary County of Hertfordshire, Hitchin Division, polling district LETCHWORTH; British Library SPR.Mic.P.16/BL.H.57. ELEVEN UNBROKEN YEARS is a man rooted in one town, and it brackets the settled period before the emigration. TWO LIMITS, BOTH STATED. The transcripts give the YEAR AND THE POLLING DISTRICT BUT NOT THE STREET — the address is on the original image and has not been read, so this does not yet date the move to 72 Pix Road. AND THE SET ENDS IN 1932, so it CANNOT bracket the 1939 departure from the English end; nothing in it reaches the years that matter for that.

rows.what: MOTA — 288 archive records, and the most important untested name
rows.note: STATED AS A GAP ON /names/ AND STILL OPEN. MOTA FIGUEIREDO is the fullest form anybody ever wrote of Ivone's maiden name — it comes from WLD 1950/1948, the first divorce — and MOTA alone returns 288 records in the archives index, far past the harvest cap used on the other spellings. NOBODY HAS READ THEM. The name is common enough that most will be nothing, but it is the one search where a relative could be hiding in plain sight under a name this archive already knows she used. NEEDS NAAIRS BACK UP — it returned 'the connection to the Search Manager Server is inactive' on the afternoon of 16 September.

rows.what: Morris Isaac Salkow — his whole litigation history, and his estate at Cape Town
rows.note: FOUND 16 SEPTEMBER BY SPELLING VARIANTS AND ONLY LOGGED, NOT WORKED. Ivone married him on 13 February 1953 and he had sued or been sued at least six times: TPD 467/1950 Rosaline born Bernhardt v him; TPD 2854/1960 him v Rosaline Burns formerly Spence-Wilson formerly Salkow; WLD 1593/1962 him v Gertie formerly Moagus; WLD 3317/1963 him v Cecilia Maud born Shein; WLD 2225/1953 him v Ivonne; and WLD 15934/1979 Mayveen Properties v him. HE MARRIED AT LEAST FOUR TIMES. AND HIS ESTATE PAPERS ARE AT KAB, MOOC 6/9/5171 ref 61416 — CAPE TOWN, where this archive ALREADY HAS AN OPEN REQUEST for the Lerena death notice. IT COULD RIDE ALONG AT NO EXTRA TRAVEL.

rows.what: Paula Luwinski sequestrated a man's estate in 1972 — and the OCR nearly made her the debtor
rows.note: OPPOSED APPLICATION. PAULA LUWINSKI VERSUS PHILLIP CRYSTAL, TAB WLD 2451/1972. Found in the variant sweep and not yet explained. THE ARCHIVE KNOWS A PAULINE LUWINSKI — Kurt's widow, born Rappoport 1914, died 1985 — AND PAULA IS NOT PAULINE, or at least is not obviously. The file is from 1972, four years after Kurt died. IF PAULA IS PAULINE UNDER A SHORTER NAME, this is the widow in court over something four years on; IF SHE IS NOT, there is a Luwinski woman in Johannesburg nobody has accounted for. EITHER ANSWER IS WORTH A ROW. It is a TAB file and belongs on any future researcher list. *** ANSWERED 16 SEPTEMBER FROM THE GAZETTE. *** Government Gazette 3701 of 10 NOVEMBER 1972, page 126, a table of sequestrations: 'No. of estate / Name and description of estate / Date upon which and division of court by which order made / UPON THE APPLICATION OF'. ENTRY T1301/72: 'PHILLIP CRYSTAL, AN ADULT WHITE MALE, A COMMERCIAL TRAVELLER, MARK HOTEL, O'REILLY ROAD, BEREA, JOHANNESBURG' — order made 17/10/72 in the Witwatersrand Local Division — UPON THE APPLICATION OF PAULA LUWINSKI. So the court file WLD 2451/1972, 'OPPOSED APPLICATION, PAULA LUWINSKI VERSUS PHILLIP CRYSTAL', is a SEQUESTRATION SHE BROUGHT AND WON. She was his creditor; he was the one living in a hotel and he was the one whose estate went. AND THE FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING. The text-extraction of that page returned the fragment 'Paula Luwinski, a commercial traveller, Mark Hotel' — the OCR had jammed two columns of a four-column table into one line, and it read as though PAULA were the commercial traveller living in the hotel. SHE WAS NOT. HE WAS. It took rendering the page as an image at 170 dpi to see the table structure, which is the same technique this archive has needed before on these scans. A COLUMN BOUNDARY IS INVISIBLE TO A TEXT DUMP. WHAT IS NOW KNOWN ABOUT HER: a Luwinski woman in Johannesburg in 1972, four years after Kurt died, solvent enough to be a creditor and determined enough to take an opposed application to judgment. WHAT IS STILL NOT KNOWN is who she was to him — she is not Pauline, whose name appears in every record as Pauline and who was born Rappoport.

rows.what: Who else sailed on the Dunvegan Castle and the Durban Castle
rows.note: CHAIN MIGRATION IS A REAL PATTERN AND IT HAS NOT BEEN TESTED HERE. The Dunvegan Castle carried 406 passengers out of London on 10 August 1939 and Martha Maud and four children were five of them. THE QUESTION IS WHETHER ANYONE ELSE ABOARD CAME FROM LETCHWORTH, HITCHIN OR BALDOCK — because people from one small town emigrating in one year usually go together or follow each other, and a neighbour on that manifest would explain WHY Johannesburg of all places, which this archive has never satisfactorily answered. Same for the Durban Castle in April. Findmypast allows browsing a voyage rather than searching a name. WORKED 16 September AS FAR AS THE INDEX ALLOWS, WHICH IS NOT FAR ENOUGH. Findmypast will browse a voyage rather than a name, and the Dunvegan Castle of 10 August 1939 returns FORTY-THREE INDEXED PASSENGERS — not the 406 the manifest states, so the indexed set is a fraction, most likely one class or one sheet. The forty-three are Bliss (two), Catto, Corbett, Coxen, Downwaite, Farber (three), Furneaux, Goldsmith, Griffin, Haward, Hay, Hobling, John, Luslie (two), Macnab and the rest, with the five Wears among them. NOT ONE OF THEM CAN BE PLACED. THE INDEXED FIELDS DO NOT INCLUDE AN ADDRESS — five Wear transcripts from this voyage were read in full earlier today and none carries one — so there is no way from the index to tell whether anybody aboard came from Letchworth, Hitchin or Baldock, which is the entire question. THE ANSWER IS ON THE IMAGE AND ONLY THERE. A BT 27 outbound form carries a column for the passenger's LAST ADDRESS IN THE UNITED KINGDOM, and that column is what would show a neighbour. SO THE ROW IS NOT DONE, IT IS RE-AIMED: view the original manifest images for both voyages — TNA BT27/1542/00/0024 for the Dunvegan Castle and BT27/1540/00/0042 for the Durban Castle — and read the address column beside the Wear entries. That is a reading job, not a search, and it is the only route to why Johannesburg.

rows.what: J. M. Dent & Sons, and the Letchworth Garden City records
rows.note: TWO INSTITUTIONAL LETTERS NOBODY HAS WRITTEN. Henry Robert Wear was a PRINTER'S ASSISTANT boarding at 9 Ridge Road in 1911 and a PRINTER'S MACHINE MINDER AT J. M. DENT & SONS at 72 Pix Road in 1921 — the Temple Press, which was the reason Letchworth existed for men like him. DENT'S BUSINESS RECORDS survive in part and staff registers sometimes name date of engagement and previous employer. SEPARATELY, THE LETCHWORTH GARDEN CITY HERITAGE FOUNDATION holds tenancy and estate records for the town's houses — both 9 Ridge Road and 72 Pix Road were Garden City property. A tenancy file would date the family's arrival and departure from the other end, independently of the passenger lists.

rows.what: Ivone's 1924 birth registration — try Lisbon, not only Maputo
rows.note: THE CENTRAL QUESTION, AND ONE ROUTE TO IT HAS NEVER BEEN TRIED. The archive has written to Mozambique and had no answer, and row 8 records eleven institutional letters still unanswered. WHAT HAS NOT BEEN TRIED IS THE PORTUGUESE SIDE OF THE SAME RECORD. Portuguese colonial civil registration was duplicated centrally, and the CONSERVATÓRIA DOS REGISTOS CENTRAIS IN LISBON holds registrations from the former overseas territories. A Portuguese assento de nascimento names BOTH PARENTS AND ALL FOUR GRANDPARENTS — far more than a South African form ever asked. SHE WAS BORN AT LOURENÇO MARQUES ON 4 MARCH 1924 and died at Porto, so she was a Portuguese national to the end and her record should exist on the metropolitan side.

rows.what: Request 18 is dead — superseded by the letter that actually went
rows.note: CLOSED 16 September. Request 18 was drafted and HELD as a separate approach to the researcher about the 1951 ante-nuptial contract. IT NEVER NEEDED TO GO. The contract is in the letter that was actually sent on 16 September — item 3 of three, LEONARD AUBREY ROBERT WEAR and MARJORIE EILEEN DUNLOP born WALKER, certificate 1397 of 1951, flagged to her as THE ONE TO GET IF SHE CAN ONLY GET ONE. Holding it as a separate letter would have been exactly the scattering Ms Xaba complained about, in a different inbox. THE FILE STAYS ON DISK as the record of an approach considered and folded into another.

rows.what: The two Giddins matches — chased the same day, and it is the wrong Giddins family
rows.note: FOUND 16 September, AND FOUND BY A GUARD RATHER THAN BY LOOKING. Publishing the newly proved Giddins generation made check:matches fail, flagging GIDDINS as a surname belonging to a living match holder. The obvious move was to call it a coincidence and add it to the ambiguous list. IT IS NOT A COINCIDENCE. TWO MATCH HOLDERS CARRY THE SURNAME GIDDINS — 43.36 cM with a twelve-person tree, and 62.89 cM with an eighty-nine-person tree and a public pedigree — AND BOTH SIT IN CLUSTER 12. THE ARITHMETIC FITS. James Giddins of Norton End, born about 1815, is Derrick's THREE-TIMES-GREAT-GRANDFATHER: James to Martha to George William Castle to Martha Maud to Leonard to Derrick. A descendant of James through Martha's brothers GEORGE b.1847 or JOHN b.1849 would be a FOURTH COUSIN, expected around 35 cM on a range that runs to 139. 43 and 63 sit comfortably inside it. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ANOTHER MATCH: every piece of DNA evidence this archive holds for the Castle side runs through GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE AND CAROLINE — the Brown cousins, the Halsey line, all of it. THESE TWO ARE THE FIRST THAT REACH ABOVE HIM, and they do it on his MOTHER'S side, which no paper record had even identified before this morning. NEXT: read the eighty-nine-person tree and look for George or John Giddins of Norton End; check whether the two Giddins matches also match each other and the Brown cousins, because if they match the Browns too the connection is through Caroline and not the Giddinses at all; and TEST THEIR SEGMENTS against the twelve-region Wear signature, which should show NOTHING — a Giddins cousin shares the Castle side only, so overlap with the Wear regions would mean the reading is wrong. *** CHECKED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CLAIM ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN. *** The larger tree — eighty-nine people, a public pedigree — was opened and read. ITS GIDDINS LINE IS WARWICKSHIRE, NOT HERTFORDSHIRE. Its GEORGE GIDDINS, 1846-1890, whose dates sat so neatly against our George b.1847, WAS BORN ON 17 JULY 1846 AT WITHYBROOK, WARWICKSHIRE and died in the Wandsworth district; HIS FATHER IS RICHARD GIDDINS, NOT JAMES. The surrounding surnames in that tree — Ratcliffe, Conway, Woodhams, Wall, McMellon, Prescott — are nowhere near Baldock. SO THE SURNAME IS NOT THE CONNECTION. The match is real — 62.89 cM is 62.89 cM — but a match holder's surname is only one of eight great-grandparental lines and there is no reason it should be the relevant one. WHAT I DID WRONG, AND IT IS WORTH NAMING: I saw a surname I had discovered that morning, found dates that fitted, and wrote three paragraphs about 'the first DNA to touch the Castle line above George William' BEFORE OPENING THE TREE. The arithmetic I did was sound and the premise was never checked. It took four minutes to check and it was wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT: two real matches at 43.36 and 62.89 cM in cluster 12, connected to Derrick for some reason that is not the Giddins surname; the smaller tree (twelve people) is too thin to read and has not been. THE HERTFORDSHIRE GIDDINSES REMAIN UNTOUCHED BY ANY DNA.

THE PLUMBING WAS ALREADY THERE AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED: index.astro has looked for hero.jpg in site/public since it was written, and its alt text ALREADY DESCRIBED THIS EXACT PAINTING — a railway running away from the viewer, winter in the foreground, dry highveld beyond, a river town at the vanishing point. rows.what: Aligned to the sibling archives — house stylesheet, fonts, grouped nav. NOT the ring.

HE IS RIGHT, AND IT IS A CORRECTNESS POINT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. The ring's own sentence reads 'each following a different line of THE SAME FAMILY'. THIS FAMILY IS HIS WIFE'S FATHER'S, out of East Prussia and Portuguese East Africa, and it meets the others nowhere.
